summary: Maya Jasanoff is a historian who studied at Harvard College (~1992–1996), Cambridge (~1996–1997), and Yale (~1997–2002). She held posts at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) and Harvard University (~2009).

Mayumi Nasu works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She held posts as lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and as specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard under Clyde Kluckhohn (~1941–1943) and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1947–1955), where he was a professor from ~1957 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and a PhD from Nanjing University, later lecturing at Colombo, BPUSL, and PGIPBS in 2008.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Johannes Rahder (1961–1962), Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells, and held a professorship at Doho University (attested 1996).

Mei Ching Hsuan works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and served as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He also served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1963 and 2007).

Meinrad Scheller was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Paris and Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, later holding professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.
Melvin Pötzsch is an Indologist and linguist who studied and held a position as a research fellow and academic staff member at the University of Marburg (attested 2026).

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington (PhD ~1961–1968) and served as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Merab Mamardashvili was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).
Mervin Viggo Hanson works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980) and studied under Kathryn A. Cissell.
Mery Cecconi is an Indology researcher who pursued PhD studies at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the doctoral supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.
Mewa Khenpo Norbu Tendzin studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Michael Alram is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. He held positions at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (1982–2020) and served as vice president of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2022).
